title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering
slides: Can Genie 4 make virtual worlds feel real?
Google's world model now generates synchronized audio.
But realism breaks down in fast-motion scenes.
Developers can already steer worlds in real time.
Test one interactive scene before assuming it scales.
thread_text:
1. The Realism Trap

Genie 4 now pairs synchronized audio with generated worlds, but fast-motion scenes still fall apart. A demo gap that could shape what ships.

2. Sound Without Sync

Google's world model finally aligns audio and visuals in real time. That's a bigger shift than visuals alone — it changes how you react to the scene.

3. Motion Breaks the Illusion

When speed increases, visuals and audio drift. The system struggles where timing matters most.

4. Steer in Real Time

Developers can already adjust viewpoints and parameters live. No need to wait for a finished world.

5. Test One Scene First

Open an interactive demo and push it to fast motion. If audio and visuals stay locked, you've found something real — if not, you know the limit.

instagram.caption:
Genie 4 now generates synchronized audio alongside its virtual worlds.

Google's world model pairs sound and visuals in real time, which changes how a scene hits you—no more silent demos guessing at timing.

But push it into fast motion and the illusion cracks: audio and visuals drift apart exactly where timing matters most.

Developers can already steer viewpoints and parameters live, no waiting for a finished world.

If you build or publish interactive content, this is testable now: open one scene, push it to fast motion, and check whether sound stays locked to the picture.

Would you ship a world where the audio starts drifting the moment things speed up? 🎧🎮🔊
